getoutofhere.text: GetOutOfHere sprays wide and wins anyway: among the very best tracked in the matchups, fast on the trigger, and standing firm when the opposition stiffens. The aim wanders, the accuracy sits near the bottom, yet the shots that land tend to land in the head. A young account, so the story is early, but the first pages are loud.

ghastl.text: ghastl is a storm of a player: matchup rating and activity both among the very best, with a relentless pace and an accuracy near the top. The edge softens a touch when the opposition gets hardest, the one wrinkle in an otherwise elite card. Lifetime numbers and matchups agree, with the lifetime IvI sitting among the very best too.

gx20.text: gx20 fights like a storm that never runs out of rain: near the top of everyone tracked, fierce no matter who shows up. Nothing rattles them against the hardest opposition. The accuracy and headshots both sit near the top, and the lifetime numbers back up the matchups. The sample behind this one is older and smaller, so take it as a sketch, not a portrait.

genialtester.text: Since 2013, GenialTester has played an efficient game: in the elite bracket, with a matchup kill-death figure near the summit. The aim sits mid-pack on the lifetime board, which makes the matchup numbers the more interesting half of the story. The lifetime ledger runs a touch cooler than the matchups, which keeps the tale honest.

glassheavn.text: Glassheavn has no weak spot, just a strong game all the way through: at the top of the matchups, unbothered by harder foes, and the edge holding strong against the strongest third. Bravery is the headline here: the harder the enemy, the stronger the showing. Lifetime numbers agree with the matchups, which makes this one a clean, complete card.

gladboystr.text: GladBoysTR brings a complete game: top shelf nearly everywhere, steady as the opposition strengthens, and sharp with every shot. The headshot rate sits near the top, and the lifetime ledger tracks the matchups closely. Treat this one as a sketch: the opponent sample behind it is older and smaller.

generallawson.text: GeneralLawson wins fights the matchup board rates among the very best, yet the aim itself sits below average and the lifetime board lands squarely mid-pack. The resistance is near the top, the bravery holds above average, and the matchup kill-death mark stays elite — results built on judgment rather than precision. A fighter whose choices, not whose crosshair, do the hard work.

gladboys.text: GladBoys thrives as the opposition gets tougher: bravery near the very top, resistance right there alongside, and a matchup mark that keeps climbing. Pace runs hot, the aim stays precise, and a strong headshot share rides along with the volume. The lifetime board rates them even higher than the matchups do, and the consistency holds up, so the whole card reads like a fighter built for the hardest rooms.

ghostonly.text: GhostOnly is a young account making a spectacular entrance: every line near the top, with headshots at the very best tracked and a lifetime board to match. Pace is relentless and the game rises with the opposition. The one wrinkle is the edge against the strongest third, which dips below average — an early read, but the first pages already carry weight.

guerrillatactics.text: GuerrillaTactics strikes fast and keeps striking: a matchup rating in the top shelf, kill pace near the very top, and bravery that holds as the opposition improves. Headshots run above average, so the volume comes with a sharp edge. The consistency mark lands mid-pack, the one dip on an otherwise strong card.

gladboysvs.text: GladBoysVS hits the field like a storm front: every adjusted line sits in the upper tier, from rating and tempo to bravery and resistance, the matchup kill-death mark keeping the same ground. The aim is razor-clean — accuracy and headshot share both top-shelf — with the lifetime numbers landing right alongside the matchups. Consistency is the one merely middling line on an otherwise relentless card.
